summary.oneLiner: RSWM Limited, the flagship textile company of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, is a globally integrated spinning-to-fabric manufacturer executing 'RSWM 2.0' — a shift from a volume-led commodity spinner to a margin-focused, vertically integrated textile enterprise.
summary.business: RSWM manufactures synthetic and performance fibres, cotton yarn and melange yarns, value-added and speciality yarns, and denim and knitted fabrics, serving fashion, activewear, home textiles and performance-led segments. It sells cotton, synthetic, core-spun, hollow-core, zero-twist, melange, eco-friendly, speciality and recycled yarns for knitting, weaving, suiting, shirting, home furnishings, carpets, sewing threads and industrial textile applications, supplying both domestic and international brand customers.

currentContext.strengths: Six-decade-old, vertically integrated manufacturing base spanning fibre, yarn, fabric and processing across 8 plant locations|Backing of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, which provides adjacent energy (Bhilwara Energy, hydro power entities) and technical-textile capabilities|Diversified, exports-led customer base across 68 countries with long-term relationships with leading domestic and international brands|Advancing renewable/green-energy profile (targeting ~70% green energy via a 60 MW round-the-clock renewable tie-up) positioned as a differentiator with global brands for whom ESG compliance is a prerequisite|Beneficiary of newly concluded India-EU FTA, India-US interim trade framework and UK-India FTA, which the company states gives it preferential market access versus Bangladesh/Vietnam competitors
currentContext.strategies: RSWM 2.0: pivot the Company from a volume-led commodity spinner to a margin-focused, vertically integrated textile enterprise, prioritising quality of earnings over scale.|Increase the share of value-added and speciality yarns across divisions (synthetic, cotton, melange) and rationalise lower-profit product lines to align production with demand priorities.|Continued equipment modernisation drive, replacing legacy equipment with contemporary variants (slub yarn, doubling yarn, compact yarn equipment).|Decisive restructuring of underperforming operations — closed the inefficient spinning division at the Chhata unit (October 2025), redeploying usable machinery to other locations and disposing of inefficient machinery.|Monetising stranded assets, including a new agreement to sell the Thermal Power Plant assets to Malik Heights.|Forward integration into recycled polyester via the LNJ Greenpet project at Ratlam, Madhya Pradesh, complementing the recycled polyester fibre operation at Ringas (operational since 2013).|Deepen the renewable/green-energy profile through the 60 MW round-the-clock renewable tie-up with Adani Green entities, targeting resilience against energy cost and carbon exposure.|Cotton Yarn division: expand the natural-fibre platform and blend-engineering capability to position RSWM as a comprehensive multi-fibre yarn solutions provider.|Melange Yarn division: intensify innovation and capacity enhancement in yarn dyeing and compact yarns to capture demand for differentiated, higher-value products.
currentContext.expansion: During FY26 RSWM expanded knit division capacity from 700 to 900 metric tonnes per month, including 120 MT of in-house printing capability, and acquired 100% equity shareholding in LNJ GreenPET Private Limited (adding a subsidiary in the recycled-fibre space). On the energy side, the Company commissioned additional ground-mounted solar installations of 3.0 MW followed by a further 7.5 MW expansion at Moradi, Banswara, taking total installed solar capacity to 48 MW, complemented by 40 MW of wind power generation; it also entered a 60 MW RERTL hybrid power purchase agreement with Adani Green Energy to strengthen its clean-energy portfolio. Looking ahead to FY27, the Company plans to further strengthen energy efficiency through expansion of automation systems and targeted operational improvements across strategically identified sites. Technology-absorption initiatives during FY24-FY26 covered modernisation across businesses: compact spinning systems, TFO and specialised equipment additions in the Yarn Business (notably at Lodha and Rishabhdev); advanced winding, dyeing and contamination-detection systems in the Melange Yarn Business; CAD/3D design technology adoption in the Denim Business; process optimisation for recycled-fibre quality in the Sustainable Textile Business; and modern dyeing machinery plus energy-efficiency upgrades in the Knit Textile Business (largely at Moradi and Chhata) — all reported as fully absorbed into regular production.
currentContext.mdna: Cotton yarn sector poised for a positive upcycle in FY27, supported by endorsement of FTAs with the UK and EU, easing US tariff pressures, and greater stability in cotton prices expected to strengthen industry sentiment and margins.|Melange division outlook for FY27 supported by the same FTA/tariff-rationalisation tailwinds, expected to drive stronger offtake of specialised yarns.|Indian spinning sector outlook is cautiously optimistic: structural shift toward man-made and blended yarns and rising demand for value-added/specialised products are expected to drive medium-term growth, while raw material price volatility and global demand fluctuations remain key risks; modernised players are gaining a competitive edge.|MMF industry outlook remains positive as global textile consumption continues shifting toward synthetic and blended fibres, supported by PLI-led investment and rising demand for performance textiles, sportswear and technical fabrics.|Denim sector maintained a positive growth trajectory in FY26 driven by domestic consumption and casualisation of apparel; premiumisation and sustainability are emerging as key differentiators, with the segment projected to grow at roughly 16% CAGR to USD 13.7 billion by FY30.|Domestic demand for cotton-based yarns showed relative resilience versus exports, supported by steady offtake from knitting, weaving and apparel segments.|Capacity utilisation across the Indian spinning sector improved gradually in the latter half of FY26 as inventory correction stabilised and demand visibility improved.|Cotton Yarn division: deepened customer partnerships led to the addition of a large global client and several others, driving a meaningful uptick in volume.|Melange Yarn division: expanded its global client base by onboarding leading international brands, driven by its capability to process naturally brown cotton fibre; also secured higher volumes from an existing garment manufacturer after enhancing VAT dyeing capability.

risks.risk: Trade-policy and tariff exposure on exports
risks.note: FY26 operating environment was marked by U.S. tariff disruptions and RoDTEP adjustments impacting the garmenting supply chain and export demand; management cites these as external headwinds that softened export demand in the first half of the year.

Domestic cotton prices remained range-bound but subject to intermittent volatility driven by global price trends, import parity and Cotton Corporation of India procurement operations, directly affecting spinning input costs.

risks.risk: Underutilised capacity / low value-added product mix
risks.note: Melange yarn utilisation stood at only 65-70% (targeted to reach 85-90% by early FY27), Knitting operated below 80% utilisation, and value-added products account for less than 20% of sales — representing structural headroom but also current margin drag if utilisation/mix does not improve as planned.

risks.risk: Revenue volatility from strategic asset rationalisation
risks.note: The closure of spinning operations at the Chhata unit removed a structurally low-margin volume source but resulted in an approximate ₹250 crore reduction in revenue, illustrating the trade-off risk embedded in the Company's ongoing portfolio rationalisation.

risks.risk: Energy and fuel cost exposure during transition
risks.note: The Company is still transitioning away from legacy coal-based boilers to biofuel-powered systems and expanding renewable power sourcing; until this transition is complete, power and fuel costs remain a variable structural exposure, even though recent initiatives have begun reducing this cost base.

thesis (one line): FY26 turnaround year — moved from a loss to positive PAT by trading volume for profitable mix, deleveraging, and shifting ~70% of energy to renewables; FY27 thesis hinges on denim/knit/melange utilisation recovery, double-digit-EBITDA aspiration, and the ₹427cr GreenPET (recycled-PET B2B) capex de-risking via a 70:30 debt-equity structure.

**One-offs:** (a) ₹23cr deferred-tax-liability reversal lifted reported PAT to ₹52cr vs ₹29cr normalised (DTL re-measured at 25.17% concessional rate vs 35%; company opts into new regime from FY27). (b) ~₹250cr revenue lost from Chhata spinning closure. (c) ₹51cr other income boosted by gain on sale of non-core assets.

**Volume / utilisation (Q4 exit):** Synthetic/fibre — optimal. Melange yarn — 65–70% (target 85–90% within 1–2 quarters). Denim — >80% (target 85–90%). Knit — <80% (target >85%). Mgmt sees 7–10% utilisation upside across denim/knit/melange in coming quarters.
guidance (critical):
- **Volume/utilisation:** denim, knit, melange each expected to improve ~7–10% utilisation off Q4 base; current quarter (Q1FY27) "slightly better or equivalent to last quarter."
- **Margin:** double-digit EBITDA is the stated aspiration "as early as possible" (no dated target); requires demand recovery + internal efficiency + product development + supply-chain sourcing combined.
- **Value-added mix:** currently <1/5 (≈20%) of sales; value-added products commoditise fast — continuous development needed; no quantified mix target.
- **Deleveraging:** ~₹700cr structured term loan (denim/knit/Banswara Kapas expansion) to be "minimised" over next 3–4 years; WC ~₹800cr being worked down.
- **Capex:** no major fresh capex beyond (i) ₹92cr knit/printing expansion (capacity 600→900 t; ~120t printing; commissioning Q3FY27; +3–4% EBITDA in knit) and (ii) ₹427cr GreenPET / recycled-PET B2B plant at Ratlam, MP (construction starts mid-May, operational Q1 next FY; funded 70:30 — ₹300cr loan approved, ₹127cr equity+holdco loan); plus routine modernisation/replacement capex (1–3 yr payback discipline).
- **Topline aspiration:** ₹6,200–6,500cr in 3–4 years deemed "possible" (analyst-led, mgmt agreed).
demand: Global textile in a "soft patch" — demand normalising, not sharply recovering; Western discretionary spend cautious. Domestic relatively resilient (₹774cr Q4 stable). Export recovery early-stage (+11.4% QoQ). US-tariff cycle disrupted garment export orders (RSWM exposure indirect — sells yarn/fabric to garmenters/weavers who export); recovery "under way," ~2 more quarters to normalcy. Inventory normalisation and better visibility in select sectors noted.
segment commentary (yarn / fabric / deni:
- **Synthetic/blended yarn:** domestic-skewed, less affected; optimal utilisation; spread maintained.
- **Cotton/melange yarn:** melange hit hardest (much is deemed-export to garmenters); util 65–70%; spreads broadly maintained.
- **Fabric/knit:** worst hit in FY26 (util <80%); ₹92cr expansion adding printing; FTAs + tariff settlement expected to drive recovery.
- **Denim:** most affected by gas disruption (lost production days in March) + cost inflation on 4–5 fronts (gas, dyes/chemicals, freight, yarn — cotton & poly-cotton); cost pass-through lags booked orders, compressing spreads; util >80%.
- **Power/captive:** ~70% of energy mix now renewable (wind/solar + Adani RTC tie-up); Adani Power ~₹1/unit saving on ~3–5 lakh units/day (~₹1cr/month); ₹60cr renewable investment cited.
- **Sustainable textile / recycled fibre:** produces 130 t/day polyester fibre from ~60 lakh recycled PET bottles/day; domestic-skewed; underpins GreenPET project synergy.
growth / optionality:
- **Value-added yarn/products:** mix <20%; commoditisation risk; continuous development thrust ("RSWM 2.0").
- **Exports / FTAs:** UK, EU, New Zealand (and Australia) FTAs are upside optionality — "yet to be reality," implementation expected late this year / early next; new markets added (Europe, Sri Lanka, 2 US denim customers).
- **GreenPET / recycled-PET B2B (Ratlam):** scaled down from ~₹700cr to ₹427cr; in-house synergy with existing recycled-fibre operations.
- **Deleveraging:** finance cost −9.2%; term-loan run-off over 3–4 yrs.
- **Knit + printing:** new product segment, +3–4% knit EBITDA from H2FY27.
margins & cost: GP margin 38.1% (+246 bps FY26) on RM-cost discipline (−9.5%) and better H2 spreads. EBITDA margin 7.1% FY26 (+231 bps). Power/fuel −₹17.6cr FY26 via renewables. Key cost pressures: gas cost stepped up sharply post-Gulf-War (availability restored by April, but price elevated), dyes/chemicals, freight, yarn prices — all squeezing denim spreads via pass-through lag. Income Tax Act 2025 → concessional 25.17% rate from FY27 (structural tax tailwind ahead).
capex:
- ₹92cr knit/printing expansion (600→900 t; commissioning Q3FY27).
- ₹427cr GreenPET recycled-PET B2B plant, Ratlam MP — land acquired, consent-to-establish obtained, construction mid-May, operational Q1 next FY; 70:30 debt:equity (₹300cr loan approved).
- Routine modernisation/old-asset-replacement capex with 1–3 yr payback discipline.
- No other major capex envisaged near term.
capital allocation (debt central): Total borrowing ₹1,510cr (from ₹1,621cr) — split ~₹700cr structured term loan + ~₹800cr working capital. Net worth ₹1,372cr → roughly ~1.1x gearing (HIGH LEVERAGE; deleveraging in progress). WC efficiency gains (inventory −₹110cr, receivables −₹65cr) freed cash. ₹36cr promoter equity infusion via 24.7 lakh convertible warrants to LNJ Textile Advisory LLP (promoter group, ~+2.5% stake) — signalling confidence. GreenPET kept majority-debt-funded to preserve balance sheet. No dividend mention. Adani Power investment within financial assets (₹387cr).
risks:
- **Commodity/cost:** elevated gas price (post-Gulf-War), volatile cotton/poly-cotton yarn, dyes/chemicals, freight; pass-through lag hurts denim/knit spreads.
- **Demand:** soft global discretionary demand; US-tariff overhang on indirect export volumes; revenue degrowth sharper than peers.
- **Leverage:** ₹1,510cr borrowings; new ₹427cr capex adds ~₹300cr debt; deleveraging dependent on cash generation.
- **Geopolitics/energy:** Gulf-War-linked gas availability/route risk; RoDTEP withdrawn for part-year; cotton import duty.
- **Value-add erosion:** value-added products commoditise quickly.
- **FTA timing:** FTAs are expectancy, not yet realised.
management tone: Confident-but-cautious; emphatic this is a genuine operational (not cyclical/optical) turnaround driven by internal actions, not market tailwinds. Candid on denim/knit pain, gas costs, value-add being <20%, and WC being higher than pure-yarn peers. Promoter warrant infusion framed as confidence signal. Repeated "RSWM 2.0", "quality of earnings over volume", "double-digit EBITDA at the earliest."
non-obvious points:
- Reported PAT ₹52cr flattered by ₹23cr one-off deferred-tax reversal → normalised ~₹29cr (margin ~0.6%); the "turnaround to profit" is real but thinner than headline.
- ~₹250cr revenue voluntarily exited (Chhata spinning) — degrowth partly deliberate, not all demand loss.
- US exposure is indirect (sells yarn/fabric to exporting garmenters) — so both the hit and recovery are second-order.
- Value-added share honestly admitted at <20% and prone to commoditisation — quality-of-earnings story still early.
- GreenPET deliberately downsized (₹700cr→₹427cr) and pushed into RSWM (vs Bhilwara Energy) for recycled-fibre synergy; kept 70% debt to avoid large equity dilution.
- Consolidated power cost < standalone due to BG Wind Pvt Ltd captive wind entity.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Gas/energy volatility → renewable (wind/solar) + Adani RTC power tie-up; BG Wind captive — beneficiaries: ⭐ RSWM's own renewable mix, Adani Power.
- US-tariff / China+1 + UK/EU/NZ FTAs → Indian textile exporters broadly (RSWM indirect via garmenters). ✅
- PET-bottle waste / sustainability mandates → recycled-PET fibre / GreenPET (RSWM). ⭐
- Income Tax Act 2025 concessional regime → structural PAT tailwind FY27+. ✅

- **Fabric/knit:** worst hit in FY26 (util <80%); ₹92cr expansion adding printing; FTAs + tariff settlement expected to drive recovery.
- **Denim:** most affected by gas disruption (lost production days in March) + cost inflation on 4–5 fronts (gas, dyes/chemicals, freight, yarn — cotton & poly-cotton); cost pass-through lags booked orders, compressing spreads; util >80%.
- **Power/captive:** ~70% of energy mix now renewable (wind/solar + Adani RTC tie-up); Adani Power ~₹1/unit saving on ~3–5 lakh units/day (~₹1cr/month); ₹60cr renewable investment cited.
- **Sustainable textile / recycled fibre:** produces 130 t/day polyester fibre from ~60 lakh recycled PET bottles/day; domestic-skewed; underpins GreenPET project synergy.
growth / optionality:
- **Value-added yarn/products:** mix <20%; commoditisation risk; continuous development thrust ("RSWM 2.0").
- **Exports / FTAs:** UK, EU, New Zealand (and Australia) FTAs are upside optionality — "yet to be reality," implementation expected late this year / early next; new markets added (Europe, Sri Lanka, 2 US denim customers).
- **GreenPET / recycled-PET B2B (Ratlam):** scaled down from ~₹700cr to ₹427cr; in-house synergy with existing recycled-fibre operations.
- **Deleveraging:** finance cost −9.2%; term-loan run-off over 3–4 yrs.
- **Knit + printing:** new product segment, +3–4% knit EBITDA from H2FY27.
margins & cost: GP margin 38.1% (+246 bps FY26) on RM-cost discipline (−9.5%) and better H2 spreads. EBITDA margin 7.1% FY26 (+231 bps). Power/fuel −₹17.6cr FY26 via renewables. Key cost pressures: gas cost stepped up sharply post-Gulf-War (availability restored by April, but price elevated), dyes/chemicals, freight, yarn prices — all squeezing denim spreads via pass-through lag. Income Tax Act 2025 → concessional 25.17% rate from FY27 (structural tax tailwind ahead).
capex:
- ₹92cr knit/printing expansion (600→900 t; commissioning Q3FY27).
- ₹427cr GreenPET recycled-PET B2B plant, Ratlam MP — land acquired, consent-to-establish obtained, construction mid-May, operational Q1 next FY; 70:30 debt:equity (₹300cr loan approved).
- Routine modernisation/old-asset-replacement capex with 1–3 yr payback discipline.
- No other major capex envisaged near term.
capital allocation (debt central): Total borrowing ₹1,510cr (from ₹1,621cr) — split ~₹700cr structured term loan + ~₹800cr working capital. Net worth ₹1,372cr → roughly ~1.1x gearing (HIGH LEVERAGE; deleveraging in progress). WC efficiency gains (inventory −₹110cr, receivables −₹65cr) freed cash. ₹36cr promoter equity infusion via 24.7 lakh convertible warrants to LNJ Textile Advisory LLP (promoter group, ~+2.5% stake) — signalling confidence. GreenPET kept majority-debt-funded to preserve balance sheet. No dividend mention. Adani Power investment within financial assets (₹387cr).
risks:
- **Commodity/cost:** elevated gas price (post-Gulf-War), volatile cotton/poly-cotton yarn, dyes/chemicals, freight; pass-through lag hurts denim/knit spreads.
- **Demand:** soft global discretionary demand; US-tariff overhang on indirect export volumes; revenue degrowth sharper than peers.
- **Leverage:** ₹1,510cr borrowings; new ₹427cr capex adds ~₹300cr debt; deleveraging dependent on cash generation.
- **Geopolitics/energy:** Gulf-War-linked gas availability/route risk; RoDTEP withdrawn for part-year; cotton import duty.
- **Value-add erosion:** value-added products commoditise quickly.
- **FTA timing:** FTAs are expectancy, not yet realised.
management tone: Confident-but-cautious; emphatic this is a genuine operational (not cyclical/optical) turnaround driven by internal actions, not market tailwinds. Candid on denim/knit pain, gas costs, value-add being <20%, and WC being higher than pure-yarn peers. Promoter warrant infusion framed as confidence signal. Repeated "RSWM 2.0", "quality of earnings over volume", "double-digit EBITDA at the earliest."
non-obvious points:
- Reported PAT ₹52cr flattered by ₹23cr one-off deferred-tax reversal → normalised ~₹29cr (margin ~0.6%); the "turnaround to profit" is real but thinner than headline.
- ~₹250cr revenue voluntarily exited (Chhata spinning) — degrowth partly deliberate, not all demand loss.
- US exposure is indirect (sells yarn/fabric to exporting garmenters) — so both the hit and recovery are second-order.
- Value-added share honestly admitted at <20% and prone to commoditisation — quality-of-earnings story still early.
- GreenPET deliberately downsized (₹700cr→₹427cr) and pushed into RSWM (vs Bhilwara Energy) for recycled-fibre synergy; kept 70% debt to avoid large equity dilution.
- Consolidated power cost < standalone due to BG Wind Pvt Ltd captive wind entity.
challenges → beneficiaries:
- Gas/energy volatility → renewable (wind/solar) + Adani RTC power tie-up; BG Wind captive — beneficiaries: ⭐ RSWM's own renewable mix, Adani Power.
- US-tariff / China+1 + UK/EU/NZ FTAs → Indian textile exporters broadly (RSWM indirect via garmenters). ✅
- PET-bottle waste / sustainability mandates → recycled-PET fibre / GreenPET (RSWM). ⭐
- Income Tax Act 2025 concessional regime → structural PAT tailwind FY27+. ✅

---
qoq log: - **Q4 FY26 (this call):** Rev ₹1,142cr (+4.5% QoQ, −9.1% YoY); EBITDA ₹85cr, margin 7.4% (+115bps YoY). FY26: Rev ₹4,554cr (−5.6%), EBITDA ₹327cr (+40.5%, margin 7.1%), PAT ₹52cr rptd / ~₹29cr norm (vs −₹41cr loss FY25) — TURNAROUND YEAR. Borrowings down to ₹1,510cr (−₹111cr). One-offs: ₹23cr DTL reversal, ₹250cr Chhata revenue exit, ₹51cr other income (asset sale). Utilisation: melange 65–70%, denim >80%, knit <80%. Capex: ₹92cr knit/printing (Q3FY27), ₹427cr GreenPET Ratlam (op. Q1 next FY, 70:30). Promoter ₹36cr warrant infusion. Guidance: double-digit-EBITDA aspiration; deleverage term loan over 3–4 yrs; Q1FY27 ≈ flat-to-slightly-better.

themes.title: Textiles - apparel/home-textile exports + synthetics
themes.need: India textiles ride three tailwinds at once: China+1 sourcing shifts, the India-UK FTA (signed) + India-EU FTA (advancing), and US tariff normalization - favouring apparel exporters (GOKEX/PGIL/PDSL) and US-heavy home-textile names (WELSPUNLIV/HIMATSEIDE). A second leg = value-added synthetics/recycling (FILATEX, SANATHAN, CENTENKA, GANECOS) and cotton-yarn spread recovery (VTL/NITINSPIN/SPORTKING) plus branded apparel (PAGEIND, ARVIND, RAYMONDLSL).
themes.driver: FTA implementation + US-India trade-deal clarity; festive/wedding demand; cotton-yarn spread; anti-dumping rulings.

hero.oneLiner: RSWM Limited, the flagship textile company of the LNJ Bhilwara Group, is a globally integrated spinning-to-fabric manufacturer executing 'RSWM 2.0' — a shift from a volume-led commodity spinner to a margin-focused, vertically integrated textile enterprise.
